title: What Happened to Hitler's Sister After the War
topic: What Happened to Hitler's Sister After the War

scenes.narration: It is the fifth of June, 1946. Berchtesgaden, high in the Bavarian Alps. An investigator working for the American Army is taking a statement from a fifty-year-old woman living in a quiet mountain inn.

Identified in military records only as Agent C10, he records that she lives in a single room, paying six marks a day. Everything she owns fits into one small suitcase. Her name is registered as Paula Wolff.
When the American investigator opened his classified file, the heading did not say Wolff. It said Paula Hitler. She was the only surviving full sibling of Adolf Hitler.
During the interrogation, she stated firmly for the record: 'I do not believe that my brother ordered the crimes committed to innumerable human beings in the concentration camps.'
What American counter-intelligence never discovered in 1946 was that during the war, Paula had been secretly engaged to Dr. Erwin Jekelius, one of the central organizers of Aktion T4.

From the Am Steinhof psychiatric complex in Vienna, over three thousand two hundred patients were dispatched to be murdered at Hartheim Castle. Among the victims was a distant cousin of the Hitler family.

Cleared of active war crimes by the denazification tribunals, Paula was left completely destitute. The Bavarian state seized all of her brother's personal estate, leaving her to rely on welfare and charity.

In 1959, she gave her only filmed interview to a British television crew, breaking years of silence. One year later, on June 1st, 1960, she died in Berchtesgaden at sixty-four, bringing the Hitler line to an end.
